calls.why: The app wanted to repeat 115/135/145/150 unchanged, but the two opening sets finished at the top of the 8-10 range last time (115x10, 135x10), so each earns one 5-lb step on the Smith bar. The top set stopped at 150x9, so 150 stays put until it gets its tenth rep, and 145 stays too - moving it to 150 would flatten the ladder into two identical top sets and make that tenth rep harder to reach.

All three sets hit 120x10 - the top of the 8-10 range on every set - and the lift is still flagged stalled, which means it has been sitting at 120 while clearing it cleanly. One 7.5-lb machine step to 127.5 is exactly what the log earned, and it is the app's own call here, so I am confirming it rather than correcting it.

Last time was 13, 12, 12 at 37.5 - inside the 12-15 range but nowhere near the top of it, so the weight has not been earned. The next pin on this machine is 45, a 20 percent jump on a small single-joint movement, so the weight holds and the target is one more rep per set. When all three reach 15, 45 is next.

70s went 14, 13, 13 - one to two reps short of the top of the 12-15 range on every set. The rack jumps straight from 70 to 80 with nothing between, so a weight step here is a 14 percent jump the log does not support. Hold 70 and chase one more rep per set; 80s come when all three sets hit 15.

Two sets cleared 25x10 and the third stopped at 9, so the ladder is nearly earned but not earned yet. The next dumbbell is 30, a 20 percent jump, which is too much to hand over for a single missing rep. Hold 25 until all three sets close at 10, then take the 30s.

The app wanted to repeat 37.5 for 15s, but at 37.5 the reps fell away to 12, 11, 10 - the last two sets landed under the slot's own 12-rep floor, so the weight is above what this slot supports. One 5-lb pin down to 32.5 puts all three sets back inside 12-15, and the load can come back up once he is finishing 15s there.
